name: Zim Laboratories Ltd
title: Zim Laboratories Ltd - 541400 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: EU-GMP still not reinstated; management guides FY27 to Rs 415-425 crore without EU and says capex is done, but H1 EBITDA margin only 5.6% and FY27 revenue guidance now implicitly raised versus prior 410-420 with EU timing slipping.

triggers.label: TGA Australia letter; first test order
triggers.quote: we have received a letter from the TGA Australia, this is an important milestone that opens up the Australian market for us

triggers.label: EU-GMP timing slipped past May
triggers.quote: we were expected in May and received the first official draft report only a month back

triggers.label: H1 pharma revenue +16%, nutra +58%
triggers.quote: For the first half, pharmaceutical revenue grew by 16% year-on-year while our Nutraceutical business grew 58% year -on-year.

triggers.label: Q2 EBITDA margin 7.3%, H1 5.6%
triggers.quote: EBITDA margin of 7.3% compared to Rs. 34 million and a margin of 3.7% in quarter 1

guidance.quote: we are looking at Rs. 415-Rs. 420 crores as the target.

guidance.value: Rs 30-40 crore on top; Rs 450-460 crore end
guidance.quote: we can put in more Rs. 30-Rs. 40 crores. So, we can look at Rs. 450-Rs. 460 crores as what we will end at.
we would be at an EBITDA margin of 18 %-20%.
it will be around 20% growth going forward for the next 2-3 years.

prior_guidance_check.quote: H2 will grow definitely, but it will grow at a 10% base of what H1 was.

So, it all depends upon the authorities.

summary.headline: Zim Labs Q2 FY27 total operating income rose 12% QoQ to Rs 1,054 mn, with EBITDA margin at 7.3%, while EU-GMP reinstatement remains the key gating item.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total operating income was about Rs 1,054 mn, up 19% YoY and 12% QoQ, and EBITDA roughly doubled QoQ to Rs 77 mn (7.3% margin) from Rs 34 mn in Q1. YoY EBITDA was flat versus Rs 78 mn, and the net loss narrowed to Rs 21 mn from Rs 40 mn in Q1. Management said the EU-GMP re-inspection draft final report is in hand, the CAPA response is with the authorities, and the TGA (Australia) letter has opened that market, with a first small test order received. Management guided FY27 to Rs 415-425 mn in operating income, with upside of Rs 30-40 mn if EU supplies begin.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 Rs 34 mn (3.7%); Q2 FY26 Rs 78 mn, flat YoY

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,462 mn (term loan Rs 841 mn, working capital Rs 621 mn)
financial_highlights.change: Term loan up from Rs 607 mn at FY26 end

financial_highlights.value: Rs 149 mn; 14% of operating income (16% incl. dossier licence fees)

financial_highlights.change: Includes Rs 45 mn for bioequivalence studies and filings

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals
segments.commentary: Contributed about Rs 830 mn, or 79% of Q2 operating income; H1 pharma revenue grew 16% YoY. Export was about 86% of Q2 operating income.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue grew 58% YoY; Unit-3 and ancillary units were shut and operations moved to the new Nutra facility.

segments.name: NIP and OTF (innovative products)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 149 mn, +84% YoY; H1 incl. licence income Rs 337 mn vs Rs 200 mn in H1 FY26 (+68%). Four marketing authorisations received in Q2 (one NIP, three OTF).

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating income target Rs 415-425 mn (management also cited Rs 425-430 mn including export incentives and licence fees), with Rs 450-460 mn possible if EU orders arrive.
Legacy/base business expected to grow about 15-20% over H1 numbers in H2 FY27 (one comment), and about 10% steady growth with ~20% thereafter.
Monthly run-rate of operating expenses expected to settle near Rs 15 mn per month after one-time EU-GMP and consultant costs (Rs 5.5 mn in H1) fall away; H1 average was about Rs 13 mn per month.
EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20% at around Rs 700 mn revenue; management said operating leverage is expected above about Rs 430-450 mn.
Commercial supplies to Australia expected in Q3 FY27; meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27 and FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 200 mn-equivalent per management's wording ('about Rs 200 crores' in the transcript) has been made, including the new Nutraceutical and Cephalosporin (CEPHA) facilities and a dedicated Pancreatin suite; gross block rose to Rs 4,188 mn from Rs 3,862 mn.
Management said no substantial capex is needed to serve orders through FY30 and no new investment is needed after EU-GMP; only operational capex for machinery upgrades.
Capacity: Rs 700 mn revenue corresponds to about 80-90% utilisation; beyond that, expansion capex may be needed 1-2 years out.
CEPHA plant started as a cost optimisation step, with easing at the old CEPHA units.
demand_pricing: Gross margin held around 57-58% (per analyst); management expects gross margin to improve once EU supplies start.
EU pipeline: 12 NIP products across 7 therapy areas and 5 OTF products across 3 therapy areas; three NIP products at end-of-procedure stage. Management plans 8-10 EU launches once EU-GMP is restored.
Pancreatin expected to lead EU revenue, with UK approval as the first market; Tamsulosin also cited. Management said contracts are signed for almost all products.

Export growth was spread across regions (LATAM, Southeast Asia, and developing Middle East and Africa); Saudi Arabia has not started commercial supplies, so no revenue loss was reported from Middle East disruption.
Management expects 5-10 new ROW product launches a month as the 48 filings convert to registrations.

qa_highlights.question: Are you on track for EU-GMP supplies from Q4 FY27 and enough EU order visibility for next year's growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the authorities' reactions require clarifications rather than further work, with responses due in a few days. UK has informally indicated that CAPA acceptance would allow supply confirmation; management said the first milestone is CAPA acceptance, then EMA process, with 1-1.5 months as a reasonable timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue target and can it reach Rs 450 mn?
qa_highlights.answer: Zain Daud said Rs 415-425 mn without EU, with Rs 30-40 mn more if EU orders arrive, so Rs 450-460 mn at the top end. Management declined to quantify beyond that, citing Middle East uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost base fall after one-time EU-GMP expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that consultant and one-time costs are not expected to recur in H2 or next year, and that a large part of the cost increase has been capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook at higher revenue levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 18-20% EBITDA margin at about Rs 700 mn revenue. It said margins could be higher but did not want to be optimistic, and will update guidance after EU supplies stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Is Rs 130-140 mn of EU revenue next year realistic and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders are in hand and EU-GMP is the only gate. Pancreatin is expected to contribute Rs 70-80 mn and Tamsulosin Rs 20-30 mn, with other products Rs 5-10 mn each, which the analyst confirmed as fair assumptions.

qa_highlights.question: What is needed for NIP and OTF to cross Rs 100 mn a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EU registration is the main trigger, which would lift NIP and OTF above Rs 20-25 mn per quarter (from about Rs 15 mn historically).

risks_watch: EU-GMP: signed final inspection report and acceptance of CAPA are still pending; timing depends on authority and EMA meeting schedules.
Operating margin: H1 EBITDA margin of 5.6% versus 8.4% a year ago; margins depend on revenue crossing about Rs 430-450 mn.
Debt of Rs 1,462 mn and rising finance costs and depreciation from the new facilities.
Middle East geopolitical uncertainty; management could not quantify the impact on H2 targets.
Management's FY27 guidance has varied across answers (Rs 415-425 mn, Rs 425-430 mn, Rs 450-460 mn) and should be tracked against the H2 print.
Dependence on a few EU products (Pancreatin, Tamsulosin) for FY28 growth.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management was confident on the EU-GMP path and order book but declined to give firm numbers beyond FY27 guidance, citing regulatory timing and Middle East uncertainty.
key_quotes: So, the milestone is not getting the EU-GMP back. The first milestone is getting the acceptance.
Today, we maintain a guidance of about 18%-20% EBITDA margin is where we are looking at.
Once the EU-GMP comes, we do not need any CAPEX.

adds.what: New Nutraceutical facility (Unit-3 and ancillary units shut, operations moved to it)
CEPHA (Cephalosporin) facility and dedicated Pancreatin suite

growth.why: FY27 operating income guided at Rs 415-425 mn (Rs 450-460 mn if EU orders arrive, i.e. +30-40 mn), with base business growth of ~15-20% over H1 run-rate in H2 and ~20% for 2-3 years; backing rests on contracts signed for EU products, 48 filings and 4 new marketing authorisations, but EU-GMP re-inspection is not yet closed and no specific new capacity with numbers was tied to the guide.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 7.3% (Q1 3.7%), with one-time EU-GMP and consultant costs (Rs 5.5 mn in H1) falling away and opex settling near Rs 15 mn/month vs H1 average Rs 13 mn; management reiterates 18-20% EBITDA margin at about Rs 700 mn revenue, though revenue is only ~Rs 420 mn run-rate for FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex of about Rs 200 crore already made (gross block Rs 4,188 mn from Rs 3,862 mn) with new Nutra facility and CEPHA commissioned; management says no substantial capex needed through FY30 to serve orders, and Rs 700 mn revenue is only at 80-90% utilisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 operating income guided at Rs 415-425 mn (Rs 450-460 mn with EU), H1 already +24% YoY at Rs 1,996 mn, base business guided +15-20% over H1 run-rate in H2 and ~20% for 2-3 years; EU orders are in hand but gated by EU-GMP.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at Rs 700 mn revenue is 80-90% and management says expansion capex may be needed 1-2 years out, but no new capex is currently planned and no-substantial-capex-to-FY30 was stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance cited as Rs 415-425 mn, Rs 425-430 mn and Rs 450-460 mn with Rs 30-40 mn EU upside; upgrade hinges on EU-GMP and CAPA acceptance, which management says takes about 1-1.5 months after the next milestone.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 5.6% vs 8.4% a year ago, H1 net loss Rs 61 mn, debt Rs 1,462 mn, and Middle East uncertainty that management could not quantify; FY27 guidance has varied across answers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans 8-10 EU launches once EU-GMP is restored, 5-10 ROW launches a month as 48 filings convert, Australia commercial supplies in Q3 FY27, and four new marketing authorisations already received in Q2 (one NIP, three OTF).

rows.label: EU-GMP re-inspection closure and CAPA acceptance
rows.why: Draft final report in hand, CAPA responses due in days, UK informally indicated CAPA acceptance allows supply confirmation; management cites 1-1.5 months to EMA process, and EU is the only gate on Rs 130-140 mn of next-year EU revenue (Pancreatin Rs 70-80 mn, Tamsulosin Rs 20-30 mn).

rows.label: Australia (TGA) commercial supplies
rows.why: TGA letter opened the market and a first small test order was received; commercial supplies expected Q3 FY27 with meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27 and FY28.

rows.label: One-time EU-GMP costs roll off
rows.why: Management confirmed consultant and one-time costs will not recur in H2 or next year, with opex settling near Rs 15 mn/month from H1 average of about Rs 13 mn after Rs 5.5 mn of H1 one-offs.

tone.note: Management was confident on the EU-GMP path, contracts signed and 18-20% margin at Rs 700 mn, but declined to quantify beyond FY27 citing regulatory timing and Middle East uncertainty; analysts pressed on FY27 guidance variance (Rs 415-425 vs 450-460 mn), margin recovery and EU revenue assumptions.
